rubrics.criterion: In the repaired cdhash.m, the embedded-signature superblob interpretation that the load-command validation walk used to perform inline (reading magic, length, and count of a locally derived CS_SuperBlob to judge the signature window's shape) is no longer re-authored as a Mach-O-side rule: either the walk no longer asks blob-shape questions at all and the existing signature parsing decides them, or the questions are answered by the code whose job is interpreting those records (the superblob/code-directory validation family used as-is or extended). A new one-off helper written next to the walk that keeps its own copy of the shape rules does not satisfy this.
rubrics.rationale: This task exists because shape policy for the embedded-signature records leaked into the header-validation layer; whether that specific leak is gone is the primary question for this instance, and it cannot be answered by generic layering review.

rubrics.criterion: In the repaired cdhash.m, the step that stages the signature for parsing (compute_cdhash_macho) no longer scouts ahead of the blob parser with its own index-table walk, its own code-directory candidate selection, and its own copy of the hash-type preference: candidate usability is decided by the blob-owning parse/ranking authority, or the pre-scan is dropped in favor of letting that authority decide as it already does after delegation. Staging keeps only file-level work: locating the signature command, translating dataoff/datasize into a window, and bounding it to the mapped image.
rubrics.rationale: The scout duplicates the blob parser's index walking and SHA-flavor ranking at the file layer; this site is the deepest instance-specific copy of that policy in the case and must be resolved, not merely relocated beside the caller.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, the superblob shape rules (magic identity, length versus available size, index-count bounds) and the hash-type preference for code directories each have exactly one interpretation site in cdhash.m — the signature-blob validation and ranking code — so tightening a bound or changing the preferred flavor is a one-place edit rather than a multi-copy audit.
rubrics.rationale: The concrete maintenance injury in this case is rule synchronization across copies; a repair that leaves the policy expressible from more than one place preserves the injury and is scored here.

rubrics.criterion: In the repaired dump.cpp, walking the signature superblob's index table, selecting the entitlement slot, and sizing the payload blob are performed by code that receives those on-disk blob structures as its contract (passed in, not derived as locals by image-walking code), and the Mach-O image class is left with image-level duties only — header identification, load-command walking, and byte-order handling — without a payload walk of its own.
rubrics.rationale: The entitlement payload interpretation sits inside the image class that owns header concerns; this instance fact is independent of the cdhash.m sites and is graded separately because the two halves can be repaired or botched independently.

rubrics.criterion: Every consumer that used to read blob fields inline is fully rewired to the shared authority: the validation walk, the delegation staging, and the entitlement extraction call the surviving interpretation instead of keeping a private reading, and no partial state remains where one site delegates while a sibling site still interprets raw fields.
rubrics.rationale: This change is cross-site by construction; a solver that repairs the first location it finds and leaves the siblings attached to their old readings is the expected failure mode this rubric isolates.

rubrics.criterion: Image-world translations stay at the image boundary: resolving the signature load command's dataoff/datasize window — including the byte order of those header-world fields and the not-in-front-of-the-header, inside-the-mapped-image window bounds — happens where the header is parsed, and the blob interpretation the repair routes to receives its region already resolved rather than re-deriving it from image fields.
rubrics.rationale: The case's two byte-swap worlds and window inequalities only make sense on the image side of the boundary; repairs that hand raw header fields to blob-side logic silently relocate image-world responsibilities, which this instance must catch.

rubrics.criterion: Singular-command behavior is preserved: code that scans load commands for the code signature still resolves at most the first LC_CODE_SIGNATURE, and no repaired path starts iterating over every signature command when the surrounding pipeline only ever consumes one.
rubrics.rationale: The pipeline's first-command semantics are a load-command-walking property that a repair can easily break by rewriting the scan; nothing generic would flag it, so it is pinned here.

rubrics.criterion: Every decline still lands as an explicit failure at the pipeline's public boundary: accepting/declining functions still translate each rejection into the failure result their callers see (a false return, an error path, or a kCopyEnt failure code), with no fall-through that turns a discarded check into a reported success.
rubrics.rationale: Rewiring early checks through new helpers is exactly the risk zone for lost failure propagation in this pipeline, and the observable contract here is the boolean result each boundary function already returns.

rubrics.criterion: No dead interpretation copy is left behind: an uncalled method, accessor, or single-caller helper that still encodes the moved-out blob rules (for instance an image-class payload extractor made unreachable by the repair, or a static shape probe kept defined but no longer called, or its commented-out remains) is present.
rubrics.rationale: Moving behavior to a new home in this instance explicitly strands the old inline copies; their presence is an instance-specific incomplete-repair signal, not a generic style complaint.

rubrics.criterion: Comments that narrate the removed inline behavior survive at the touched sites, describing blob probing or scouting behavior that no longer exists there.
rubrics.rationale: The injected sites carried inline design commentary tied to their local shape; stale narration after behavior relocation is specific to this instance and it misdirects future maintenance.

rubrics.criterion: Half-moved wiring remains at any repaired site: locals that existed only to support the old inline reading (derived blob pointers, bounds helpers, or early-exit flags) survive unused or vestigial in the calling code.
rubrics.rationale: The old inline copies were built on local scaffolding specific to this instance; left-behind scaffolding is direct evidence the extraction was not completed.

rubrics.criterion: The decision boundary is unchanged: every input the pre-repair pipeline declines stays declined (corrupt or out-of-range signature window, unusable superblob shape, no usable candidate hash flavor), every accepted binary yields the same cdhash bytes as before, and entitlement payloads that were extracted before are still extracted byte-identically, including images inside fat containers.
rubrics.rationale: Behavioral outcomes over the recorded decision axes are the hard safety contract of this case; they are finer-grained than suite-level pass/fail and must be verified as preserved by any sound repair.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired pipeline contains an early (pre-parse) path that newly declines an input the embedded-signature parsing accepts, widening the rejection set beyond what the current pipeline or the signature-blob code rejects.
rubrics.rationale: Early-decline hardening in this pipeline is contractually a subset of the parse's own rejections; strictness drift in either direction is the instance's characteristic regression.

rubrics.criterion: Byte-order integrity survives the move in both files: header-world fields (magic, load-command, dataoff) resolve under the detected image swap state they were already resolved with, while on-disk signature-blob fields resolve the way the blob helpers treat them (network order in cdhash.m, the file-static swap in dump.cpp), with no access re-homed to the other discipline.
rubrics.rationale: Two coexisting swap disciplines across the exact boundary this repair crosses is the sharpest silent-corruption risk in this instance and is invisible without domain inspection.

rubrics.criterion: The public surface is altered: the signatures of compute_cdhash, find_cdhash, or copyEntitlementDataFromFile change, or a kCopyEnt* result code is renamed, renumbered, or reinterpreted so an existing caller would observe a different result.
rubrics.rationale: These are the concrete external seams this instance promised to keep stable; verifying them requires knowing this pipeline, which no generic checklist would.
